› Explain how the approval prompt works before you touch anything

• When a command needs approval, Codex draws an overlay. The headline reads
  "Would you like to run the following command?", the reason and the command
  itself follow, and then it lists the choices:

  1. "Yes, proceed" — runs the command once and continues the turn.
  2. "Yes, and don't ask again for commands that start with `echo`" — records
     an execpolicy amendment for that prefix.
  3. "No, and tell Codex what to do differently" — cancels and hands the turn
     back to you so you can redirect.

  You answer with enter, or press esc to cancel. Nothing is running right now,
  so there is no dialog on screen — I was only describing one.
